purpose: Generated reference mockups; not production UI

concepts.name: 1 — Studio-Porträt
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE highly finished raster desktop WEBSITE UI concept screenshot, wide landscape approximately 1600x1000 or 1920x1200, flat front-on screen capture, no monitor/device frame, no presentation labels, no multiple variants in one image.
References: image 1 is the actual existing portfolio website and is the spatial/layout context. Preserve its dark brick arcade room, slim top header, and full claw machine with the existing purple-shirt cartoon puppet at the LEFT occupying about 28% of the view. Redesign ONLY the large About content area on the RIGHT, about 70% of the view. Keep the hall visible around that content. Image 2 is the exact person/identity reference for Dennis's photographic portrait: preserve his recognizable wavy dark brown hair, brown eyes, beard, facial proportions, smile and black ribbed turtleneck. Use a clean realistic head-and-shoulders crop; IGNORE any colored stripes or damaged transparent-background pixels around the person in that reference. Do not turn the photographic portrait into a cartoon. Images 3 and 4 are actual NEXUS and Lowlight work samples, use them only where the direction calls for actual project thumbnails, not as whole-page styling references.
Art direction: genuinely authored designer portfolio, modern sleek futuristic but HUMAN, exceptionally controlled composition and typography. Remain near-black/charcoal with warm off-white text, natural warm skin, tiny cool pearl/ice/lavender iridescent material accents. NO full rainbow, no HUD, no cyberpunk circuitry, no holographic face, no fake metrics or RPG stats, no visual clutter, no tiny generic avatar, no generic grid of rounded SaaS cards. The face must be a major focal point visibly much larger than the old avatar. Typography remains crisp plausible real web type, refined Outfit-like sans, with strong size contrast. All copy must be short, well-spaced and readable, never filler.
Existing header text: DENNIS; Projekte; Über mich; Kontakt; DE / EN; MENÜ. Cabinet title: ÜBER MICH.
Permitted About content, verbatim as needed: "ÜBER MICH", "Offen für Freelance", "Dennis", "Bierreth-Fernandez", "Art Director · UX/UI · Product Builder", "Ich gestalte Marken, digitale Erlebnisse und eigene Produkte.", "Art Director bei Floordirekt", "6+ Jahre Agentur & Inhouse", "Mannheim / Heidelberg", "Kontakt", "LinkedIn", "Art Direction", "UX/UI", "Eigene Produkte", "NEXUS", "Lowlight", "Werdegang", "2025 – heute". Do not add slogans or random wording. Retain a slim, elegant bottom station navigation with previous "Kontakt" and next "Riftback", small restrained iridescent orientation line. No dense CV table or skill-chip wall. Important content and contact must be immediately visible. This is a design mockup, not implementation.
DIRECTION A: QUIET EDITORIAL STUDIO PORTRAIT. Make a deliberate asymmetric two-column opening INSIDE the right content panel: left text about 53%, right portrait about 47%. Large "Dennis" with smaller beautifully set "Bierreth-Fernandez" beneath, restrained role line, then the short positioning sentence and Contact / LinkedIn. A large photographic HEAD-AND-SHOULDERS portrait occupies the upper-right, mounted behind clear lightly smoked photographic glass, a precision thin ice-lavender light seam along only two edges echoing the physical claw machine window. Face is warm, clear and naturally lit; no milky layer or reflection over eyes. Portrait field about 420px high, visible face about 220px wide, tight enough to be powerful. Black sweater fades subtly into charcoal. The photograph reaches close to top/right panel margins. Below the shared hero, 3 spacious open typography-led competency columns "Art Direction", "UX/UI", "Eigene Produkte"; two slim image samples below the latter show actual NEXUS and Lowlight, no large cards. At lower edge a concise Floordirekt / experience line. Rich but understated tactile material, beautiful optical spacing and hierarchy. Composition balanced, calm, confident and distinctly unlike the old resume panel.
